reference.title: Dumbbell Close grip Press
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower the dumbbells to the chest, exhale as you press.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.2 s up

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9). Expect to use less than for a regular dumbbell press: the narrow grip gave the lowest 6RM loads in Saeterbakken 2021.
prescription.progression: More reps, a 1 s pause on the chest, then the next dumbbell.

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench, feet planted; press the dumbbells up with the palms facing each other and the two dumbbells touching along their length.
Breathe in and lower them together to the middle of the chest, elbows tucked close to your sides.
Dumbbells touch the lower chest lightly, still pressed against each other.
Breathe out and press up, squeezing the dumbbells together the whole way.
Arms straight over the chest, dumbbells still touching; reset and go again.

mistakes.fix: Squeeze them together hard the whole set; that squeeze is what loads the chest.
Keep the elbows close to the ribs, about 15-30 degrees from the body.

mistakes.mistake: Lowering to the neck or the belly
mistakes.fix: Lower to the middle of the chest, with the forearms angled in toward the dumbbells.
Stack the wrists straight over the forearms.

kinematics.norm: Neutral, dumbbells pressed together (clinical opinion). A narrow grip increased triceps activity in the barbell press (Saeterbakken 2021; Muyor 2023)
Arms straight at the top; at the bottom the dumbbells touch the chest with the elbows about 90-100 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow tuck (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: Elbows close to the ribs, about 15-30 degrees from the body (clinical opinion)
Up and down over the middle of the chest, dumbbells together (clinical opinion)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020 (head, shoulders and hips on the bench)
Controlled; Muyor 2023 paced 2 s up and 2 s down with a metronome

sources.title: GymVisual #029612, Dumbbell Close grip Press, video (movement reference)

Saeterbakken, Stien, Pedersen, Solstad, Cumming and Andersen 2021, the effect of grip width on muscle strength and electromyographic activity in bench press among novice- and resistance-trained men (Int J Environ Res Public Health 18(12):6444; PMC8296276)

Muyor, Rodríguez-Ridao and Oliva-Lozano 2023, comparison of muscle activity between the horizontal bench press and the seated chest press exercises using several grips (J Hum Kinet 87:23-34; doi 10.5114/jhk/161468)

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)

cautions: Get into position safely: sit on the end of the bench with the dumbbells on the thighs, then lie back and kick them up one knee at a time; at the end of the set bring them back to the thighs or lower them to the floor beside the bench rather than dropping them (clinical opinion).
Hold the dumbbells firmly together over the chest; use fixed-plate dumbbells.
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; bent-back wrists under a heavy dumbbell strain the wrist.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist discomfort: let the dumbbells separate a few centimetres.
Shoulder discomfort: shorten the range so the dumbbells stop just above the chest.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Presses the arms up and squeezes them together. Grip width did not change overall pectoralis activity in the barbell bench press (Saeterbakken 2021), although the sternal (middle) fibres were less active with a narrow (50% of shoulder width) barbell grip in Muyor 2023.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Presses the arms up and squeezes them together. Grip width did not change overall pectoralis activity in the barbell bench press (Saeterbakken 2021), although the sternal (middle) fibres were less active with a narrow (50% of shoulder width) barbell grip in Muyor 2023.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder; its activity did not differ between narrow and wide grips (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder; its activity did not differ between narrow and wide grips (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Main elbow extensor: triceps activity was higher with a narrow barbell grip than a wide one (Saeterbakken 2021; Muyor 2023: about 16% vs 12% of MVIC at 50% vs 150% of shoulder width).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Main elbow extensor: triceps activity was higher with a narrow barbell grip than a wide one (Saeterbakken 2021; Muyor 2023: about 16% vs 12% of MVIC at 50% vs 150% of shoulder width).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Less active with a narrow grip than a wide one (Saeterbakken 2021); still steadies the elbow under the free weights.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Less active with a narrow grip than a wide one (Saeterbakken 2021); still steadies the elbow under the free weights.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the dumbbells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the dumbbells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the seat.

guides.label: Press up over the mid chest
Elbows tucked, about 90-110 at the bottom
